one_liner: Train on rater-disagreement-preserving labels instead of consensus: does keeping disagreement improve calibration more than it costs accuracy?
problem: Medical segmentation datasets collapse multiple expert opinions into one consensus mask, discarding the disagreement structure that encodes true ambiguity.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: models trained on the full rater distribution (sampling raters per example, not averaging) produce uncertainty maps that match held-out expert disagreement far better than consensus-trained models with post-hoc uncertainty, at <2 Dice cost - the disagreement is learnable signal, not noise.
why_important: Clinical decisions need to know WHERE experts would disagree; consensus training makes models confidently arbitrary exactly there.
why_possibly_novel: Multi-rater modeling exists (KNOWN: probabilistic U-Net line of work); the specific calibration-vs-Dice tradeoff quantification against held-out raters across modalities is less established. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: LIDC-IDRI (4 raters): train consensus vs rater-sampling models, evaluate uncertainty against held-out rater disagreement maps.
main_risk: Rater identity confounds (systematic rater styles) may dominate genuine case ambiguity.

one_liner: CT models secretly depend on window/level preprocessing conventions: randomized windowing collapses them, revealing intensity brittleness.
problem: CT pipelines bake in windowing presets (e.g. soft-tissue window). Models may learn the preset, not the anatomy, making them fragile to any acquisition/preprocessing change.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: state-of-the-art CT segmenters lose disproportionate Dice under clinically-plausible window/level perturbations (which preserve all diagnostic information a radiologist needs), and a model trained window-agnostic recovers the gap with no in-distribution cost - proving the fragility is a preprocessing artifact, not a capacity limit.
why_important: Windowing varies across hospitals and PACS exports; this is a silent, ubiquitous deployment shift nobody benchmarks.
why_possibly_novel: Windowing as a formal domain-shift axis with an information-preservation argument is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Take 3 public CT models, sweep window/level within radiologically-valid ranges, plot degradation; retrain one with randomized windows.
main_risk: Some windows genuinely destroy information for specific organs; must define validity ranges with a radiologist.

one_liner: Slice-direction inconsistency of 2D models on 3D volumes scales with through-plane anisotropy: derive the consistency-spacing law.
problem: 2D slice-wise segmentation (including SAM-based) produces jagged 3D shapes. How inconsistency scales with slice spacing/anisotropy has not been formalized, so nobody knows when 2D is 'good enough'.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: inter-slice mask inconsistency grows linearly with slice spacing up to an organ-dependent correlation length, beyond which 2D and 3D models converge in quality - giving a per-organ spacing threshold that predicts when 3D context stops helping.
why_important: Answers the perpetual 2D-vs-3D question with a measurable law instead of anecdote, guiding architecture choice per dataset.
why_possibly_novel: An explicit anatomical correlation-length framing of the 2D/3D tradeoff is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Downsample isotropic CT volumes to various spacings, train/evaluate matched 2D and 3D models, fit the crossover per organ.
main_risk: Confounded by training-data volume differences between 2D slices and 3D patches; must match supervision bits.

one_liner: MedSAM-style box prompting leaks organ-size priors: models segment the expected organ size, failing on pathological sizes.
problem: Box prompts encode expected extents. Medical models fine-tuned with GT boxes may learn organ-size priors that break precisely on the abnormal cases that matter clinically (atrophy, hypertrophy, tumors).
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: MedSAM-style models' error grows sharply with an organ's deviation from population-median size (controlling for boundary difficulty), and prompting with deliberately wrong-size boxes drags predictions toward the box size - demonstrating prior leakage that inflates benchmark scores on normal anatomy while hiding failure on pathology.
why_important: Clinical value concentrates in abnormal cases; a size prior is exactly the wrong inductive bias, and current benchmarks (mostly normal-ish anatomy) cannot see it.
why_possibly_novel: Size-deviation-stratified evaluation of promptable medical models is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Stratify public organ datasets by size percentile, plot Dice vs deviation; run wrong-box perturbation response curves.
main_risk: Extreme sizes correlate with genuinely harder boundaries; needs matched-difficulty controls.

one_liner: Is ultrasound speckle noise or signal? Despeckling ablation to test whether models use speckle texture as anatomical cue.
problem: Speckle is treated as noise to be removed, but speckle statistics are tissue-dependent - models may rely on it as discriminative texture, in which case despeckling harms segmentation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: segmentation models trained on raw ultrasound lose significant accuracy when tested on despeckled inputs (and vice versa), and per-tissue analysis shows speckle statistics carry class information comparable to boundary information for homogeneous organs - speckle is signal.
why_important: Resolves a preprocessing controversy with direct consequences for every ultrasound pipeline and for cross-device generalization (speckle is device-dependent).
why_possibly_novel: Information-content quantification of speckle for segmentation (not detection/denoising) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train/test 2x2 (raw/despeckled) on CAMUS + thyroid datasets; add a texture-only probe (boundary-masked patches) for class information.
main_risk: Results may be despeckling-algorithm dependent; use 3 different filters.

one_liner: Stain normalization in pathology helps less than stain-diverse training: an assumption audit with controlled compute.
problem: Stain normalization is near-universal in computational pathology, assumed necessary for cross-lab transfer. Modern augmentation/diverse pretraining may have made it redundant or harmful.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: at matched compute, stain augmentation dominates stain normalization for cross-site segmentation transfer, and normalization actively destroys discriminative chromatic information for some tissue classes (measurable per-class sign flips).
why_important: Normalization is a preprocessing tax on every pathology pipeline; if it is obsolete or harmful, the field should know. KNOWN: augmentation-vs-normalization comparisons exist in classification contexts; segmentation-specific and per-class sign analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
why_possibly_novel: Per-class harm analysis of normalization for segmentation, rather than aggregate AUC comparisons.
minimal_experiment: CAMELYON-derived segmentation with multi-site splits: 2x2 normalization/augmentation factorial at matched budgets.
main_risk: Conclusions may not transfer across stain types (H&E vs IHC); scope both.

one_liner: Text-report-derived weak labels vs 5 minutes of scribbles: the annotation-economics showdown for medical segmentation.
problem: Two weak-supervision currencies compete - mining radiology reports (free but noisy/indirect) vs minimal expert scribbles (costly but spatial). Their exchange rate has never been measured.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per unit of final Dice, expert scribble-seconds outperform report-derived labels by an order of magnitude for spatially-precise structures, but report labels win for presence/coverage of diffuse pathology - the modality of weak supervision must match the spatial statistics of the target.
why_important: Hospitals sit on millions of reports; knowing when they are worth mining vs when to just pay for scribbles is a real resource-allocation question.
why_possibly_novel: A quantified exchange rate between supervision types under matched outcomes is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On a chest CT dataset with reports, train (a) report-mined weak labels, (b) budget-matched scribbles, (c) mixtures; compare Dice-per-dollar curves.
main_risk: Report-mining quality depends heavily on NLP extraction quality, a moving target.

one_liner: Tumor boundary uncertainty is directionally structured (infiltration axes); isotropic uncertainty models are wrong in a measurable way.
problem: Infiltrative tumors grow along anatomical corridors (white-matter tracts, tissue planes), so true boundary ambiguity is anisotropic - but every uncertainty method outputs isotropic per-pixel variance.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: held-out multi-rater disagreement on glioma boundaries is significantly anisotropic (aligned with local tissue orientation), and current uncertainty methods' outputs are near-isotropic - a representational mismatch that directional evaluation will expose and that matters for radiotherapy margins.
why_important: Radiotherapy margin expansion is currently isotropic partly because tools are; demonstrating structured anisotropy could change margin design.
why_possibly_novel: Directional decomposition of segmentation uncertainty against anatomical orientation fields is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: BraTS-style multi-rater subset + DTI atlas orientations: measure disagreement anisotropy; compare uncertainty-method outputs directionally.
main_risk: Multi-rater glioma data with enough raters is scarce; may need to commission a small re-annotation.

one_liner: Longitudinal self-supervision: same-patient scan pairs give free consistency labels that beat generic pretraining for segmentation.
problem: Hospitals have massive longitudinal archives (same patient, months apart) that are unused for pretraining; stable anatomy between visits is a free correspondence signal stronger than augmentation-based SSL.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: pretraining with cross-visit anatomical correspondence objectives (predicting stable vs changed regions without registration GT) transfers to downstream segmentation better than in-modality SimCLR/MAE at matched data and compute, especially for small-structure Dice.
why_important: Uses data hospitals already have with zero extra annotation; targets the medical-specific structure (longitudinal stability) generic SSL ignores.
why_possibly_novel: Longitudinal-pair pretraining for dense medical tasks appears under-explored. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Assemble public longitudinal MRI (ADNI/OASIS), pretrain correspondence vs MAE at matched compute, fine-tune on hippocampus/lesion segmentation.
main_risk: Registration shortcuts could let the model cheat; objective design must prevent trivial solutions.

one_liner: Partial-label multi-dataset training silently teaches 'organ X is background': quantify negative-transfer from unlabeled structures.
problem: Combining datasets where each labels different organs means every dataset actively teaches that other organs are background - a contradiction that everyone works around ad hoc.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: naive multi-dataset training suppresses each organ's recall proportionally to how often it appears unlabeled in partner datasets (a measurable dose-response 'background poisoning' curve), and the effect size exceeds architecture-choice effects in typical setups.
why_important: Multi-dataset training is how everyone scales medical models now; an unmeasured poisoning law means the ecosystem's scaling curves are bent by label sociology, not learning capacity.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: partial-label learning methods exist (e.g. marginal losses); the quantified dose-response poisoning law is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Controlled mixes of 3 abdominal datasets with disjoint labels; vary the fraction of poisoning images per organ, fit recall vs poisoning-dose.
main_risk: Effect confounds with dataset appearance shift; use single-source synthetic label-hiding as the clean control.

one_liner: Vessel and airway models optimize Dice but break topology: measure the Dice-topology Pareto frontier and show current models sit at its wrong end.
problem: For tubular structures, a 1-voxel break destroys downstream use (flow simulation, navigation) while barely moving Dice; the field optimizes and reports the wrong quantity.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: across public vessel/airway models, topology error (Betti number mismatch, broken-branch count) is nearly uncorrelated with Dice above Dice=0.8, and models selected by validation Dice are strictly dominated on the topology axis by differently-selected checkpoints of the SAME training run - the problem is checkpoint selection, not capacity.
why_important: If correct, large topology gains are available for free (different model selection), and benchmark rankings for tubular tasks are misleading.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: clDice and topology losses exist; the checkpoint-selection reframing (topology is lost at selection time, not training time) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Retrain a standard vessel model, log Dice and topology metrics for ALL checkpoints, test whether topology-selected checkpoints dominate.
main_risk: May be true only near convergence for specific architectures; test 3 architectures.

one_liner: Find the through-plane spacing threshold where 3D convolution stops beating 2D - a reusable crossover law for the field.
problem: Whether to use 2D, 2.5D, or 3D models is re-litigated in every medical paper without a governing quantitative rule.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: the 3D-over-2D Dice advantage decays monotonically with slice spacing normalized by structure diameter, crossing zero near spacing~0.5x structure diameter, consistently across organs and modalities - a dimensionless law that predicts the right architecture from dataset metadata alone.
why_important: Would eliminate a whole genre of redundant ablation studies and guide architecture choice from acquisition parameters.
why_possibly_novel: Dimensionless scaling analysis (spacing/diameter) for the 2D-3D question is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Resample 5 isotropic datasets to a spacing grid, train matched 2D/3D models, fit the crossover in dimensionless units.
main_risk: Anisotropic acquisition artifacts (slice profile, gap) differ from clean downsampling; validate on natively anisotropic data.

one_liner: Annotation fatigue leaves order signatures in public medical datasets: label quality drifts within annotation sessions and is detectable post hoc.
problem: Medical labels are made by humans in long sessions; fatigue and drift should leave statistical traces (boundary quality vs slice index / case order), but no one audits datasets for it.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: in public volumetric datasets, boundary smoothness and model-vs-label disagreement vary systematically with slice order within volumes (start vs end of stacks) and with case ID order, revealing session-position effects large enough to bias per-region evaluation (e.g. organ ends are labeled worse).
why_important: If label quality is spatially/temporally structured, benchmark errors attributed to models are partly annotation fatigue - affecting especially the apex/base slices clinicians care about.
why_possibly_novel: Forensic fatigue analysis of existing datasets (no new labels needed) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: For 5 public datasets, regress label-quality proxies (curvature statistics, inter-slice coherence, model consensus disagreement) on slice position and case order.
main_risk: Proxies for 'label quality' without re-annotation are indirect; commission spot re-annotations for validation.

one_liner: Low-level statistics distance (power spectrum, noise model) predicts MedSAM transfer failure better than semantic/anatomical distance.
problem: Foundation medical models fail unpredictably on new modalities/protocols. The community assumes semantic novelty drives failure; it may be mundane signal statistics.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: transfer performance of promptable medical models across 20+ dataset pairs is predicted (r>0.7) by low-level statistics divergence (radially-averaged power spectra, noise floor, intensity histogram transport cost) and only weakly by anatomy/modality labels - most 'domain gap' is signal-processing gap.
why_important: A cheap pre-deployment compatibility test from unlabeled images, plus redirection of adaptation research toward signal harmonization.
why_possibly_novel: Systematic low-level-vs-semantic attribution of medical transfer failure is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Evaluate MedSAM/SAM across the modality grid of public datasets, regress performance drops on statistics divergences vs semantic dummies.
main_risk: Low-level and semantic distances correlate across natural dataset pairs; needs synthetic-perturbation legs to break the confound.

one_liner: Clinician clicks differ from simulated clicks: measure the sim2real prompting gap that inflates interactive medical benchmarks.
problem: Interactive medical segmentation is evaluated with simulated prompts (center-of-error clicks). Real clinicians click based on anatomical salience and diagnostic habit, not error geometry.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: real clinician click distributions differ measurably from simulators (clicks favor anatomically meaningful landmarks and avoid ambiguous tissue), and evaluating with real click traces drops reported model performance by a clinically meaningful margin, reordering methods - simulator choice is a hidden hyperparameter of the entire subfield.
why_important: If benchmark rankings do not survive real users, the field is optimizing simulator-fit; protocols must change before clinical deployment claims.
why_possibly_novel: Collected clinician-click corpora for evaluation replay are rare/absent. UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Record 3 clinicians x 100 cases of real interactive use, replay traces against 4 models, compare with simulator-based rankings.
main_risk: Small-N clinician study; click styles may vary more between clinicians than between simulators (itself a finding).

one_liner: Contrast-polarity invariance test: can one model segment T1 and T2 (inverted tissue contrast) without contrast-specific features, and what does it cost?
problem: MRI sequences flip which tissue is bright. Models either specialize per sequence or are claimed 'sequence-agnostic' without a controlled test of what invariance costs.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: enforcing polarity invariance (training with random contrast inversions consistent with tissue physics) costs little on seen sequences but roughly doubles zero-shot transfer to unseen sequences - i.e. most cross-sequence failure is polarity/contrast coding, a low-dimensional and fixable factor, not anatomy understanding.
why_important: Sequence proliferation is the main practical obstacle to universal MRI models; identifying the failure as low-dimensional makes it tractable.
why_possibly_novel: Physics-consistent contrast-inversion invariance analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Train on T1 with physics-based contrast remapping augmentation, test zero-shot on T2/FLAIR; compare against multi-sequence-trained upper bound.
main_risk: Some pathologies are only visible in specific sequences; invariance may erase pathology signal - stratify by lesion visibility.

one_liner: Below a lesion-size threshold, segmentation-first pipelines beat detection-first: locate the crossover.
problem: Tiny lesion pipelines either detect-then-segment or segment-then-group. Which paradigm wins at which size regime is undocumented, so teams choose by habit.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: per-lesion recall of detection-first pipelines collapses below a size threshold (relative to receptive-field stride) where dense segmentation-first retains sensitivity, producing a crossover point measurable in voxels that generalizes across modalities when normalized by resolution.
why_important: Metastasis screening and microbleed detection live exactly in the tiny regime; the field needs the regime map.
why_possibly_novel: Head-to-head paradigm comparison stratified by object size in physical units is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: On microbleed/metastasis datasets, run matched detection-first and segmentation-first pipelines, plot per-lesion recall vs size.
main_risk: Implementation quality asymmetry between paradigms could masquerade as a paradigm effect; use strong tuned baselines for both.

one_liner: Extreme class imbalance has a phase transition: below a foreground-fraction threshold, per-lesion recall decouples from Dice and both metrics stop constraining each other.
problem: At foreground fractions below ~0.1%, standard metrics and training dynamics enter a regime the field treats with the same tools as moderate imbalance; whether this regime is qualitatively different is untested.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: as foreground fraction decreases, there is a measurable transition where (a) the correlation between Dice and per-lesion recall across checkpoints drops toward zero, and (b) training becomes bimodal (models either find lesions or ignore them entirely, seed-dependent) - a phase structure implying different evaluation and early-stopping rules are needed in the extreme regime.
why_important: Screening applications live in the extreme regime; if metric decoupling and seed-bimodality are real, current papers' single-seed Dice claims there are close to meaningless.
why_possibly_novel: Phase-transition framing with checkpoint-level correlation analysis is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Synthetic imbalance ladder (subsample lesion voxels progressively), train 10 seeds per level, measure metric decoupling and outcome bimodality.
main_risk: Transition may be gradual, not sharp - report as regime change rather than critical point if so.

one_liner: Simulate cross-vendor MRI shift from k-space physics and test how much of the real vendor gap physics-only augmentation closes.
problem: Cross-vendor generalization is attacked with generic augmentation or adaptation, but vendor differences are substantially physics (k-space filtering, coil combination, reconstruction) that can be forward-simulated.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: augmenting a single-vendor training set with physics-simulated vendor transforms closes >60% of the measured cross-vendor Dice gap, and the residual gap localizes to protocol (not reconstruction) differences - decomposing 'vendor shift' into simulable and non-simulable parts.
why_important: Would replace data-hungry multi-vendor collection with physics simulation for a large fraction of the problem, and produce the first quantitative decomposition of vendor shift.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: MRI physics augmentation exists in reconstruction literature; the segmentation-gap decomposition claim is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Use multi-vendor brain datasets, implement k-space filter/noise/bias-field simulation, measure gap closure per component.
main_risk: Faithful vendor simulation requires proprietary details; approximate simulation may cap the closure fraction for reasons unrelated to the hypothesis.

one_liner: Probe-pressure deformation is the dominant unmodeled augmentation for ultrasound: geometric, physics-parameterized, and testable.
problem: Ultrasound anatomy deforms under operator probe pressure. No standard augmentation models this; models may fail across operators simply due to compression states.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: a biomechanically-plausible compression augmentation (depth-dependent anisotropic strain) improves cross-operator segmentation transfer more than any standard photometric/geometric augmentation at matched strength, because compression is the leading axis of real operator variation.
why_important: Operator dependence is ultrasound's defining weakness; naming and modeling its main geometric factor would be broadly reusable.
why_possibly_novel: Compression-specific augmentation validated on cross-operator splits is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Datasets with repeated sweeps by different operators (or phantom studies): augmentation ablation over cross-operator splits.
main_risk: Cross-operator datasets are scarce; a phantom + small clinical validation may be the only path.

one_liner: Benchmarks reporting Dice above the inter-rater ceiling are fitting annotator style: audit which medical leaderboards have crossed their own noise floor.
problem: Each dataset has a Dice ceiling given by expert-vs-expert agreement. Leaderboard scores near or above single-rater agreement indicate style overfitting, not superhuman accuracy - but ceilings are rarely computed or compared.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: several prominent medical segmentation leaderboards have SOTA scores within noise of (or above) the inter-rater ceiling for their structure types, and the models' residual 'errors' correlate with rater-style dimensions rather than anatomy - meaning further leaderboard progress there is epistemically empty.
why_important: Redirects effort away from saturated benchmarks and toward datasets/metrics with real headroom; protects clinical claims from style-fitting artifacts.
why_possibly_novel: Cross-benchmark systematic ceiling audit is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search (individual inter-rater studies are KNOWN).
minimal_experiment: Collect published inter-rater figures per structure, compare with leaderboard SOTA; for 2 datasets, commission small re-rating to measure style-vs-anatomy error decomposition.
main_risk: Published inter-rater numbers use varying protocols; harmonization needed before comparison.

one_liner: Anatomy-relative coordinates transfer prompts across patients: one expert prompt reused on a thousand scans.
problem: Promptable models need per-image prompts. In medical imaging, anatomy provides a shared coordinate system that could let one prompt (defined relative to landmarks) transfer across patients - turning interactive into automatic segmentation.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: prompts expressed in anatomy-normalized coordinates (via cheap landmark detection, no deformable registration) retain >90% of per-patient manual-prompt Dice on organs with stable topology, and the transfer failure cases are exactly the clinically abnormal anatomies - making prompt-transfer failure itself an anomaly detector.
why_important: Amortizes expert interaction across cohorts (huge for population studies), and the failure-as-anomaly-signal is a free second product.
why_possibly_novel: Prompt-space anatomical normalization (rather than image registration) is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Abdominal CT cohort: define prompts on 5 template patients, transfer via landmark alignment, measure retained Dice and abnormality enrichment among failures.
main_risk: Landmark detectors fail on the same abnormal cases, entangling the anomaly signal.

one_liner: Site fingerprints in federated medical segmentation: features encode hospital identity, and removing it costs accuracy - measure the privacy-performance coupling.
problem: Features of medical segmentation models may encode acquisition-site identity (scanner, protocol), which is simultaneously a privacy leak, a shortcut-learning risk, and possibly useful signal. The three roles have not been jointly quantified.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: site identity is linearly decodable from mid-level features of standard models with high accuracy; enforcing site-invariance degrades in-site accuracy only marginally but improves cross-site transfer - i.e. the site code is mostly shortcut, not signal, and its removal is nearly free.
why_important: Directly informs federated learning design and shortcut mitigation in the setting where regulatory stakes are highest.
why_possibly_novel: KNOWN: site effects in radiomics are documented; the joint decodability-invariance-transfer quantification for segmentation features is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Multi-site public data (e.g. multi-site prostate MRI): site probes on features, invariance-constrained retraining, transfer matrix comparison.
main_risk: Site correlates with population case-mix; invariance may remove genuine epidemiological signal - needs case-mix controls.

one_liner: Volume measurements inherit uncalibrated uncertainty from segmentation: are downstream tumor-volume confidence intervals valid even when masks look good?
problem: Clinical endpoints are derived quantities (volumes, diameters), yet uncertainty is evaluated at pixel level. Pixel-calibrated models can still yield badly mis-calibrated volume estimates because errors are spatially correlated.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: volume confidence intervals derived from per-pixel uncertainties are anti-conservative by large factors (2-5x too narrow) because pixel errors are positively correlated along boundaries, and a boundary-correlation-aware propagation restores near-nominal coverage without changing the model.
why_important: RECIST-style measurements drive treatment decisions; invalid CIs are a direct clinical safety issue that pixel metrics cannot reveal.
why_possibly_novel: Coverage analysis of derived clinical quantities from segmentation uncertainty is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Multi-rater lesion datasets: compare nominal vs empirical coverage of volume CIs across uncertainty methods; measure boundary error correlation lengths.
main_risk: Multi-rater 'true volume' is itself uncertain; use synthetic lesions with exact GT as the anchor condition.

one_liner: Consensus fusion (STAPLE-style) systematically erases minority-expert detections that are disproportionately correct on rare pathologies.
problem: Multi-rater fusion assumes the majority is right. For rare or subtle findings, the specialist minority may carry the correct signal, and consensus training deletes it.
core_hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS: on cases with confirmed outcomes (pathology/follow-up), regions flagged by exactly one expert (majority-rejected) contain true findings at a rate far above chance and concentrated in rare disease subtypes - so consensus-trained models are structurally biased against the rare cases that matter most, in a measurable, outcome-anchored way.
why_important: Challenges the default label-fusion practice for the exact case class (rare, subtle) where AI assistance is most valuable.
why_possibly_novel: Outcome-anchored audit of minority-rater regions is UNVERIFIED - needs lit search.
minimal_experiment: Dataset with rater annotations + outcome verification (e.g. screening cohorts with follow-up): measure precision of minority-only regions vs chance.
main_risk: Outcome-linked multi-rater datasets are rare and access-restricted; may require collaboration for data.
